note: Coordinates a human has pinned, because the geocoder found a different place of the same name. Every entry carries a reason; an override without one is indistinguishable from a typo. The check gate refuses those.
why: The resolver walks a place phrase from longest to shortest — «Arienzo, Caserta», then «Arienzo» — and a miss on the full phrase followed by a hit on the bare name is exactly how you get the wrong town. Those are reported as `loose` by the importer so a human can look.

arienzo.why: The comune of Arienzo in the province of Caserta. The geocoder matched a hamlet of the same name near Salerno, 44 km south — right country, wrong town, and nothing in the build gate could have seen it.

benevento.why: The city of Benevento. The geocoder returned a point 14 km north, which is the province rather than the town.

senja.why: Sv. Juraj of Senj, on the Kvarner coast, and the one case here where the wrong town was found by reading a CASE ENDING as a name. The waypoint «Senja, Sv. Juraj» is a genitive — Sv. Juraj, of Senj — and read as a nominative it matched Senja in Serbia, which exists, 450 km away. The six Roman Catholic registers under it begin in 1695 and come from collection 2040054, «Croatia, Church Books, 1516-1994»; that Serbian ground was Ottoman until 1718 and kept no Catholic parish. Pinned to the gazetteer's Sveti Juraj, 6.9 km from Senj, which puts it back inside the kvarner region and its archive, Državni arhiv u Rijeci.

somerset.why: The English county of Somerset, which is the D'Arcy archive's ground — Chew Magna and Bristol. The geocoder chose a Somerset in Los Angeles County, California, 8,500 km away, because the bare name matches eighteen places in the United States alone.

grad.why: Grad in Prekmurje, Slovenia, not the Grad in Dalmatia. The FamilySearch path for all ten volumes is «Vas > Felsőlendva» — Felsőlendva is the Hungarian name of this Grad, in Vas county — and the collection is «Slovenia, Prekmurje and Međimurje, Civil Registers, 1895-1918», Hungarian-titled (Születtek, Házasultak, Halottak). The point it carried was a population-zero Grad 368 km away, which also put it inside the dalmatia record region and gave it Dalmatian eras it never had. Pinned to the gazetteer's Grad, SI, 46.7976,16.0984 (pop 686), in Prekmurje.

tisina.why: Tišina in Prekmurje, Slovenia. The path is «Vas > Tissina»: Hungarian civil registers filed under Vas county. The Croatian Tišina (Kaptolska) it carried was in Croatia-Slavonia, a separate kingdom, 127 km from Prekmurje, and cannot appear in a Vas county register. Pinned to the gazetteer's Tišina, SI, 46.6542,16.0936 (pop 412).

turnisce.why: Turnišče in Prekmurje, Slovenia. The path is «Zala > Turnischa»: Hungarian civil registers filed under Zala county, which included the Lendava district. The Croatian Turnišće it carried is 150 km from Međimurje, the part of Croatia that was in Zala. Pinned to the gazetteer's Turnišče, SI, 46.6257,16.3139 (pop 1,509).

svjakovsiljevica.why: Sv. Jakov-Šiljevica, now Jadranovo, on the Kvarner coast, not a Šiljevica in central Serbia. The register is Roman Catholic, in «Croatia, Church Books, 1516-1994»; the gazetteer's Jadranovo (pop 1,077) lists «Sveti Jakov Siljevica» among its alternate names. Pinned to the gazetteer's Jadranovo, HR, 45.2311,14.6183.

bale.why: Bale (Valle d'Istria) in Istria, Croatia, not a Bale in Montenegro 503 km away. Eight Roman Catholic volumes in «Croatia, Church Books», some from 1538; the place already carried «Valle» and «Valle d'Istria» as names, and Valle is Bale's Italian name. Pinned to the gazetteer's Bale, HR, 45.0406,13.7836 (pop 973).

klasnic.why: Klasnić, in the Glina area of Croatia, not a Klašnić in central Serbia. The register is Orthodox, in «Croatia, Church Books». The gazetteer holds two villages, Donji Klasnić (45.2293,16.1636) and Gornji Klasnić (45.2375,16.1378), 2.5 km apart, and nothing in the path says which, so the point is the midpoint between them and not either village. Pinned to the midpoint of Donji and Gornji Klasnić, HR.
